sents.t: Tonight, I’m sitting in the window of Sunrise Bakery with a cup of coffee and an old notebook.
It’s the notebook that I bought on my first day in Oakville.
On the first page, in big, careful letters, I wrote: “Hello. My name is Sam. I am new here.”
I’ve been writing in it ever since.
The first pages are full of mistakes, and I used to be embarrassed by them.
I have survived snowstorms, a flat tire, a hurricane, and a letter from the IRS.
I’ve run a half marathon, hosted a podcast, and helped a seventy-eight-year-old woman become a citizen.
I’ve learned that a piece of cake isn’t always cake, and that home isn’t always the place where you were born.

The people here have taught me more than any textbook: Rosa, who opened her door; Mr. Lee, who gave me a chance; Carlos, who taught me to drive; Emma, who believed in my work; and Lily, who is going to be my wife.
If someone asked me for advice, I would say: Don’t wait until your English is perfect.
Lily is turning off the lights now, and Max is waiting at the door.
Tomorrow, I’ll start a new notebook.

o: in the window of Sunrise Bakery

comp.q: When did Sam buy the notebook?
o: on his first day in Oakville
comp.fa: سام کی آن دفترچه را خرید؟

comp.q: How does Sam feel about his early mistakes now?
o: He wants to throw the notebook away.
comp.fa: سام حالا درباره‌ی اشتباهات اولش چه احساسی دارد؟

comp.q: What is Sam’s advice for English learners?
o: Wait until your English is perfect.
Make mistakes and laugh at them.
comp.fa: توصیه‌ی سام به زبان‌آموزان انگلیسی چیست؟

comp.q: What does “Tomorrow, I’ll start a new notebook” suggest?
o: Sam will keep learning and writing.
comp.fa: جمله‌ی «Tomorrow, I’ll start a new notebook» چه چیزی را نشان می‌دهد؟
